title: Ordering, Installing and Removing Meters Under the Metering Service
content:
**Ordering.** A **Metering Service** meter type may be ordered only for a service agreement whose rate schedule is among the type's supported schedules and whose capabilities the agreement needs: a time-of-use schedule needs a time-of-use capable meter, a demand schedule needs a demand register, a net energy metering agreement needs a bidirectional meter, and service at primary voltage needs the Primary Metering Installation.

**Installation date.** The installation date is no earlier than the meter type's installation lead time, in business days, after the order date.

**In service and removal.** The installed meter becomes in service on its installation date, and the meter it replaces is removed the same day.

**Withdrawal and reuse.** An order may be withdrawn while it is scheduled. A removed or cancelled installation is never reused; a later need is met by a new order.

## Installation statuses

| Status | Meaning | Moves to |
|---|---|---|
| Scheduled | Ordered, not yet installed | In service, when the field crew installs the meter and it starts registering for billing; or cancelled, when the order is withdrawn before installation at the customer's request or because the service start was cancelled |
| In service | Registering for billing | Removed, when the meter is taken out of service for exchange, shop testing, an opt-out or return, or because the service agreement closed |
| Removed | Out of service | Never reused |
| Cancelled | Order withdrawn | Never reused |

## Capability needs (worked from the rule)

| The agreement has | The meter ordered must be |
|---|---|
| A time-of-use schedule | Time-of-use capable |
| A demand schedule | Fitted with a demand register |
| A net energy metering agreement | Bidirectional |
| Service at primary voltage | The Primary Metering Installation |

**Hypothetical case.** An agreement on Schedule RT Residential Time-of-Use Service is a time-of-use agreement, so the meter type ordered for it must both list Schedule RT among its supported schedules and be time-of-use capable.
